full_judgment: 3. The defendant bank contested the suit by filing written statement denying the alleged contract for sale of the disputed land stating, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable and the same was barred by limitation. Their further case is that the bank acquired title in the disputed land on the basis of mortgage given by Sarada Paul. Subsequently Sarada Paul with the help of other gentlemen of the locality, interested in education, started a Primary School on 0.05 acre of land to the eastern side of the disputed plot. One Indra Kumar became the Headmaster of the school. Headmaster's residence was constructed on an area of 0.01-1/2 cents of land to the western side of the school building. Indra Kumar was never the bharatia under Sarada Paul. Plaintiffs husband Sitanath did never take bhara from said Indra Kumar. Plaintiff husband on the death of Indra Kumar became the Headmaster of the school and started residing at the Headmaster's residence mentioned above. Subsequently the school was aided by the local municipality and the Government. Some local persons had expressed their desire to purchase some other land from the bank, but the bank authority informed them that without approval of the Government and without permission of their Head Office it was not possible to sell the land. The plaintiff also expressed her desire at that time to purchase 0.01-1/2 decimal of land covered by the residence of the said Headmaster where she had been residing along with her husband and with a view to showing her desire to purchase such land, in case the same would be sold by the bank, she, of her own accord, deposited with the bank a sum of Tk. 100/- although no contract for sale was made by the bank with the plaintiff. The defendant bank kept the said deposited money in their blocked account. The bank authority also applied for permission to dispose of some of their landed property but the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla refused to accord permission to dispose of such land.
